page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz without multi-threading, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The hardware layout includes a 48 MB L3 cache and integrated local storage consisting of a 237 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. No discrete GPU acceleration is included in this instance configuration.

Benchmark results show notable strengths in memory throughput and compression workloads. The PassMark memory test achieves a top-tier rating with a score of 3831.3, supported by uncached memory read bandwidth of 123.64 GB/sec. Compression performance is prominent, with single-threaded gzip compression achieving 36.53 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression hitting 17.27 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10 percent. Standard computational benchmarks such as stress-ng register mid-tier performance across single-core (2010.29) and multi-core (8022.08) runs.

Tradeoffs center around raw mathematical and specialized computing tasks. The PassMark overall CPU score ranks in the lower quartile at 5627.95, along with weaker relative performance in cryptographic tests. Additionally, large language model prompt evaluation is restricted, reaching only 11.29 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model. These metrics reflect architecture optimization geared toward standard enterprise operations rather than compute-bound vector processing or deep learning.

The qualitative cost-efficiency profile of the m9gd.xlarge is advantageous for operations that extract value from combined local NVMe I/O and high memory bandwidth without paying for unneeded accelerator silicon. It is well suited for web serving, microservices hosting, caching nodes using its 13.22 million operations per second Redis throughput, intermediate ETL processing, and transactional database scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V3 architecture. Running on the Nitro system, it provides 4 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz, 16.0 GB of memory, and 237 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage with a 2 Gbps network baseline. Performance benchmarks highlight exceptional memory throughput and compression capability, with top-tier results in PassMark memory testing and single-threaded gzip processing. Standard processing metrics, such as stress-ng and static web throughput, remain consistent with mid-tier enterprise profiles, while compute-heavy cryptography and LLM prompt processing exhibit lower relative throughput. The absence of SMT ensures predictable per-core execution. With its bundled low-latency local storage and balanced 1:4 core-to-memory distribution, the m9gd.xlarge is designed for distributed microservices, caching applications, lightweight databases, and continuous integration pipelines.
